beats.text: Same kids, same job. Then in July, the Canada Child Benefit deposit changed. Nobody called. It happens every year.
The benefit year runs from July to June. Every July, the CRA recalculates it from last year's tax return.
So payments from July twenty twenty-six use your twenty twenty-five family income.
Priya's family went from sixty thousand to seventy thousand in twenty twenty-five. That raise lands on the benefit now, in July.
Reason two: the amounts are indexed to inflation. The maximum for a child under six went from seven thousand nine hundred and ninety-seven to eight thousand one hundred and fifty-seven dollars.
The twist: the benefit always runs a year behind your life. Lose income this year, and it only shows up next July.
So when July looks different, check last year's return, not this year's paycheque.
Next: the GST credit got a new name, and who gets it. Follow so you don't miss it.
